subject.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle for Telegram and WhatsApp

question: Which parts of the durable-ingress implementation should become a permanent public plugin SDK contract in this PR?
rationale: The architectural consolidation is plausible, but publishing claim-owner and retry helpers creates a long-lived compatibility commitment that cannot be inferred from contributor preference or tests alone.

options.title: Approve a smaller public seam
options.body: Expose the drain factory, lifecycle binding, queue types, and drain type while keeping claim-owner and retry-policy internals core-owned until external consumers demonstrate a stable need.

options.title: Approve the proposed seam
options.body: Accept all currently listed helpers as supported plugin API and own their compatibility, documentation, and future deprecation path.

options.title: Keep the drain bundled-only
options.body: Land the core and bundled-channel consolidation without a new public SDK contract, then design the external seam separately.

recommendation.title: Approve a smaller public seam
recommendation.body: Expose the drain factory, lifecycle binding, queue types, and drain type while keeping claim-owner and retry-policy internals core-owned until external consumers demonstrate a stable need.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on explicit plugin SDK boundaries and surface budgets makes this the strongest available routing signal for the API-contract decision.
